{{Quote|The Republic's Great Manifest period (20,000&ndash;17,000 BBY) marked an increased movement into the Rimward territories of the Slice, which became known as the Expansion Region.|From the text of ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' by [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]]|<ref name="NEC" />}}
The '''Great Manifest Period''' of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] was a span of [[Time/Legends|time]] that lasted from [[20,000 BBY/Legends|20,000 BBY]] to [[17,018 BBY]]. It was characterized by increased movement into [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] and the establishment of the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]] in its [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Rimward]] territories. Even as the Republic expanded [[Astrography|astrographically]], the government expanded its [[Politics/Legends|bureaucracy]]. The [[Rule of Fifty|limit]] of fifty [[Star system/Legends|systems]] per [[Sector/Legends|sector]] that had been set by the early Republic continued to be ignored, causing already burgeoning sectors in the newly colonized areas of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Realspace/Legends|space]] to be virtually ungovernable. Additionally, the era featured the creation of the [[Metellos Trade Route/Legends|Metellos Trade Route]], which connected [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to [[Metellos/Legends|Metellos]] and other points west of the [[Galactic Center|galactic center]]. The new [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|route]] increased trade among the newly connected systems. Around 2,000 years thereafter, the bureaucracy expanded with the establishment of the [[Bureau of Ships and Services/Legends|Bureau of Ships and Services]] to regulate and manage transportation across the [[galactic community]].

Culturally, the Republic was undergoing change, as well. [[Vianism]], a religion that had developed among the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], became non-extant on its generative [[Planet/Legends|planets]]; however, it spread into the expanding regions of the galaxy and took hold within the [[Kanz sector/Legends|Kanz sector]]. Additionally, the famed [[Shawken Spire]] saw its destruction during the Great Manifest Period, an event that was [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy|remembered]] [[10,000 BBY|over 8,000 years later]]. All the while, outside of Republic space, the two planets [[Neona]] and [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] underwent dramatic climate changes. These events, which began during the Great Manifest Period, caused extinction for the [[Unidentified Neona species|native species]] of Neona and forced adaption of the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] species. Nevertheless, the era and its corresponding boom were brought to an abrupt end by internal strife in the form of the [[First Alsakan Conflict]].

==Proem==
{{SeeAlso|Expansionist Era}}
Following the creation of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Expansionist Period/Legends|Expansionist Era]] featured steady but limited growth to Republic [[Realspace/Legends|space]] until its terminus in [[20,000 BBY/Legends|20,000 BBY]]. Most of the known [[galactic community]] was confined to the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] and other [[Planet/Legends|planets]] that lined the existing [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|routes]] of the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] and the early legs of the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]]. Outside of Republic space, however, interstellar alliances, such as [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]], the [[Herglic Trade Empire]], and the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]], existed along with numerous yet-unknown, but inhabited, worlds.<ref name="EA" />

As the years passed, the Republic continued to expand. Exploration into the regions colloquially known as "[[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]]" and the blazing of new hyperspace routes were regarded as dangerous endeavors. The risks notwithstanding, the Republic was expanding into the area of space that later became known as "[[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]]." By 100 years before the Great Manifest Period began, many worlds in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] and [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] had been settled.<ref name="EA" /> Additionally, some cultures had begun [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Rimward]] migration during this time. Among them, the [[Etti]] had fled the Core Worlds as a reaction to persecution at the hands of the what they viewed as the Republic's oppressive and tyrannical government. These people had [[Terraforming/Legends|terraformed]] the planet [[Etti IV/Legends|Etti IV]] and relocated outside of the Republic boundaries&mdash;and [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] [[Politics/Legends|bureaucracy]].<ref name="SotES">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==The galaxy during the Great Manifest Period==
===Commerce and politics===
====Early expansion and bureaucratic growth====
The Great Manifest Period of the Galactic Republic began in 20,000 BBY. Planets such as [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]], [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], and [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] continued the trend of expansion and settlement deeper into "the Slice," populating the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]]. The colonization and expansion had become institutionalized during this time, with companies and planets vying for resources and settlements. Corellia and Coruscant were able to stake claim to the choicest locations along hyperspace routes, however, prompting resentment to brood on Alsakan. Within the Slice proper, colonists and corporations from Alsakan and Coruscant aggressively competed for new [[Star system/Legends|systems]] in which to establish their hold, while Corellia largely staked its claim south of the [[Galactic Center|galactic center]].<ref name="EA" />

About 20,000 BBY, the Core World planet [[Metellos/Legends|Metellos]] was experiencing the domestic problems of overpopulation and a lack of trade. The planetary government commissioned a new hyperspace route to connect eastward, to Coruscant, with the intent of easing its struggle.<ref name="CCW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref> Additionally, the planet hoped that the new hyperspace route would extend west of the Core in a manner analogous to the super-routes of the Perlemian Trade Route and the Corellian Run, which connected far-flung regions of space with the Core.<ref name="EA" /> When the route reached its completion, the new [[Metellos Trade Route/Legends|Metellos Trade Route]] connected eastward to Coruscant as desired,<ref name="CCW" /> but the trail only extended westward to [[Orooturoo]] due to anomalous eddies within hyperspace west of the Core. Ultimately, trade with Coruscant marginally increased, but commercial traffic saw the most growth between Metellos and Orooturoo.<ref name="EA" />

As the Republic burgeoned, so did its bureaucracy. With the growth of Republic space, new [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] were created and gained representation in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], increasing the size of the governing body. Existing sectors also grew, in spite of the "[[Rule of Fifty]]"&mdash;a Republic law designed to limit the number of [[Star/Legends|star]] systems in a single sector at fifty. As the growth of the Great Manifest Period continued, the rule was largely ignored, and some sectors became so large that they were rendered ungovernable.<ref name="EA" />

The expansion of the Republic, combined with the increase in hyperspace travel and commerce among its member worlds, prompted the creation of the [[Bureau of Ships and Services/Legends|Bureau of Ships and Services]] (BoSS).<ref name="EA" /> The organization, created within the bureaucracy of the Republic, was designed to track movement of [[Starship/Legends|ships]] and goods through space, along with assigning [[Transponder code/Legends|transponder codes]] and tracking vessel ownership.<ref name="PSG">''[[Platt's Starport Guide]]''</ref> The BoSS was said to have been created more than 1,000 years prior to the end of the Great Manifest Period,<ref name="EA" /> although it had also been remarked that the Bureau was created slightly later.<ref name="PSG" />

====Prelude to conflict====
As the Great Manifest Period unfolded, the differences between Core stalwarts Coruscant and Alsakan reached a pivotal juncture. Cultural and socio-political differences in the Core were being reflected in the Rimward reaches of the Republic. The citizens of Alsakan and daughter colonies neither viewed the Republic as the pinnacle of achievement nor aligned with large mega-corporations. They preferred and retained a more aristocratic philosophy and sought for less bureaucracy and greater local or planetary independence. At the same time, Coruscant and its corporate-political interests sought to attain a foothold as much of the Slice as possible in an effort to amass a stockpile of natural resources. The Slice largely divided into an Alsakani-dominant northern portion, including worlds along the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]], and a Coruscant-controlled southern half that became known as the "Exploitation Region."<ref name="EGW" />

The corporate conglomerates of Coruscant aggressively pushed further into the Rimward systems and acted against the Alsakani colonial efforts in their exploitation of the new-found worlds. The merchants evicted many of the colonists, who took refuge in Alsakani-aligned worlds along the Perlemian. Alsakan's envy of Coruscanti control, combined with a belief that the Republic was both too strong and centralized, prompted a deeper colonization campaign. Alsakan-led warships accompanied colonial efforts on resource-rich worlds, to which the so-called "[[Grand Companies]]" resisted. As a result, armed freighters of Duros merchants skirmished with the Alsakani vessels. The Coruscant-based Republic government backed its corporate interests and open conflict began in [[17,018 BBY]] with the Republic [[Republic assault on Virujansi|assault and capture]] of the Alsakan colony [[Virujansi/Legends|Virujansi]].<ref name="EGW" />

===Culture===
The early years of the Great Manifest Period marked the end of the religion [[Vianism]] within the Core Worlds. Vianism was an ancient belief system that originated in the Core Worlds and centered on worship of the goddess [[Via]] and her two likeness: the [[Beatific Countenance]] and the [[Glorious Radiance]]. Even though the religion died out in the Core, it was retained among the ancestors to the [[Argazdan/Legends|Argazdan]] civilization. These peoples then sent missionaries throughout the worlds of the [[Kanz sector/Legends|Kanz sector]], where the religion was revived with the conversion of the [[Lorrdian/Legends|Lorrdians]] and [[Sipsk'ud]].<ref name="DSPL">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/fiction/feature20090531/index.html?page=1|text=Death in the Slave Pits of Lorrd: A Hyperspace Exclusive|int=Death in the Slave Pits of Lorrd}}</ref>

On the Core World [[Shawken]], the massive structure known as the [[Shawken Spire]] had reached low-[[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] altitudes. Made from ancient building materials since its foundations over 700 years prior, the structure had grown in renown across the known galaxy. In [[18,780 BBY]], the iconic edifice that predated the Republic met its destruction.<ref name="EA" /> Also in the Core Worlds, the competition between Alsakan and Coruscant spilled over into linguistic usage. Alsakan was promoting the usage of the [[High Galactic (language)|High Galactic]] language and [[High Galactic/Legends|alphabet]], in place of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] and [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]], which were used on Coruscant.<ref name="WW">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref>

Prior to the year [[19,000 BBY]], a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] named [[Humat]] became insane and left the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Upon dropping out of the Order, he fled with his most valuable treasures to Coruscant. There, Humat buried his belongings in a deep underground vault that became known as the [[Cell of Imu]]. Within the locale were numerous types of technology that were protected by traps and skeletons that had been [[Dark transfer|animated]] by use of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] [[Sith sorcery/Legends|magic]]. The centerpiece of his collection was a talisman known as the [[soul stealer]].<ref name="CCW" />

===Outside of Republic space===
During the early years of the Great Manifest Period, two planets outside of Republic space underwent significant climatic changes.<ref name="EA" /> Around [[19,997 BBY]], in what later became the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]], the [[Water/Legends|ice caps]] of the planet [[Neona]] began to melt and flood the surface. As the surface became submerged, its [[Unidentified Neona species|native]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] was driven to extinction.<ref name="LotE">''[[Lords of the Expanse]]''</ref> At the time, the worlds of the Tapani sector were unknown to the broader Republic, although they were within the reach of the [[Herglic Trade Empire]].<ref name="EA" />

Similarly, the Wild Space planet of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] began a climate shift around 19,000 BBY. There, the surface ice of the planet's glaciers began to melt. The low-lying marsh areas and narrow [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] began to flood, forcing the native [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]] from their native homelands. Over time, the land area became completely submerged, and the Kaminoans were forced to live above the rising water levels. As with Neona, the event took place on a world that had yet to have been discovered by the Republic.<ref name="EA" />

==Impact==
{{Quote|While the fighting never expanded to a full-scale civil war in the Republic, the first of the Alsakan Conflicts ended the boom of the Great Manifest Period. However, it did not end Alsakan's ambitions, and the Alsakanese would continue to attempt to claim their "rightful" place as galactic capital for another 14,000 years.|[[Doctor/Legends|Dr.]] [[Milanda Vorgan]]|<ref name="WW" />}}
The expansion and colonization efforts of the Great Manifest Period came to an abrupt end in [[17,018 BBY]] with the outbreak of the [[First Alsakan Conflict]].<ref name="EA" /> Approximately [[17,012 BBY|six years after fighting began]], Alsakan liberated the Virujansi. [[First Alsakan Conflict|War]] continued for more than three hundred years with battles at [[Battle of Kes|Kes]], [[First Siege of Porus Vida|Porus Vida]], and [[Siege of Belasco|Belasco]].<ref name="EGW" /> [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Seventeen conflicts]] occurred in all, [[Seventeenth Alsakan Conflict|culminating]] in [[3017 BBY]]. The conflicts caused desolation in the Slice with long-lasting effects. Since the battles were primarily fought among the colonial holdings in what was later termed the Expansion Region, the area of the Slice near the Perlemian Trade Route was left sparsely populated compared to the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|area of space]] near the Corellian Run where Corellia had continued its expansion unabated. War effected galactic culture, as well as historical landmarks, such as the [[Alsakan Mosaics]] and [[Belgoth's Beacon]], which were destroyed during the battles.<ref name="EA" /> The onslaught of war also prompted the Corellians to insert the ''[[Contemplanys Hermi]]'' clause into the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]], allowing themselves to be recused from open conflict between Coruscant and Alsakan in spite of the sympathies to Alsakani beliefs. This created, at times, three ''de facto'' independent states during the periods of conflict.<ref name="EGW" /> The constitutional clause was invoked on later occasions by Corellia in its attempts for secession.<ref name="HNN:CCB">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|47|news/13314_1.html|Corellia Closes Borders}}</ref>

Not only did war affect the Republic, but the creation of the Bureau of Ships and Services had a permanent effect on transportation and commerce throughout the galaxy. The immense organization grew to have outposts on numerous worlds and kept records of nearly every starship transaction. It also regulated aspects of trade among worlds of the Republic. Because of its size, the BoSS developed its own unique culture and language. It became a nuisance for [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], who often sought ways around BoSS regulations and observers. Even in the years approaching the Galactic Civil War, the Republic, and later the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], avoided confrontation with the extra-planetary organization.<ref name="PSG" /> The BoSS also controlled the [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Flare stick|beacon]] system, which was used as leverage by the organization to quell the First Alsakan Conflict in [[16,700 BBY]].<ref name="EGW" />

Even though Vianism died out in its generative worlds of the Core during the early Great Manifest Period, the religion continued in the Kanz sector. Having been brought to these far reaches by the ancestors to the Argazdan peoples, Vianism continued to flourish, and it remained in place even until the Galactic Civil War. Among the branches of Vianism that formed were the [[Sisterhood of the Glorious Radiance]] and the [[Myrialites]]. The changes in religion helped facilitate the ethnic strife between worlds in the sector, leading ultimately to the [[Kanz Disorders/Legends|Kanz Disorders]].<ref name="DSPL" /> Cultural changes continued linguistically, as well. The language Galactic Basic Standard, and its Aurebesh alphabet became the ''lingua franca'' of Republic worlds rather than the Alsakanese language; although, High Galactic retained usage among nobility and clergy, and the alphabet survived even until the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="WW" />

Sometime after the collapse of the Shawken Spire, the task was undertaken to rebuild it. The reconstructed edifice, however, was built with more modern materials, contrasting with the materials that had previously graced the structure. The iconic building continued to be remembered through time, as well. In celebration of the Republic's founding, the historian [[Vicendi]] was commissioned to complete a list of [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy|twenty galactic wonders]]. The Shawken Spire was included as one of the wonders within his [[10,000 BBY]] publication, ''[[Arturum Galactinum]]''.<ref name="EA" />

With their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] having underwent dramatic climactic changes that began in the Great Manifest Period, the Kaminoan civilization adapted to the changing surroundings. Eventually, the Kaminoans abandoned their former [[City/Legends|cities]], such as [[Derem City]], as the surface flooded. While architectural wonders like the [[Clock Spires of Harai Nova]] became submerged, the Kaminoans adapted their technology to move their cities to stilts above the rising water level. They also turned to [[Bioengineering/Legends|genetic engineering]] to preserve the flora and fauna that drowned in the planetary flooding. [[Geneticist/Legends|Genetics]] and [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] later became a feature of Kaminoan technology.<ref name="EA" />

==Timeline of the Great Manifest Period==
*c. [[20,000 BBY/Legends|20,000 BBY]]<ref name="EA" />
**The Galactic Republic's Great Manifest Period began<ref name="EA" />
**The [[Metellos Trade Route/Legends|Metellos Trade Route]] was created by the [[Metellos/Legends|Metellos]], resulting in minor trade with [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], but significantly greater trade with [[Orooturoo]]<ref name="CCW" />
*After [[20,000 BBY/Legends|20,000 BBY]]<ref name="DSPL" />
**[[Vianism]] died out in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] but spread throughout worlds in the [[Kanz sector/Legends|Kanz sector]]<ref name="DSPL" />
*c. [[19,997 BBY]]<ref name="LotE" />
**[[Neona]] underwent a dramatic climate change that caused the surface to become submerged underwater<ref name="LotE" />
**The native species of Neona was driven to extinction as a result of the climate change<ref name="LotE" />
*Before [[19,000 BBY]]<ref name="CCW" />
**An insane Jedi named [[Humat]] left the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], fleeing with his treasures to Coruscant and burying them deep underground in a vault that became known as the [[Cell of Imu]]<ref name="CCW" />
*c. 19,000 BBY<ref name="EA" />
**[[Kamino/Legends|Kamino's]] glaciers began to melt due to climate change<ref name="EA" />
*[[18,780 BBY]]<ref name="EA" />
**The [[Shawken Spire]], a super-tall structure on [[Shawken]] that reached low-orbit altitude, was destroyed<ref name="EA" />
*By [[18,000 BBY]]<ref name="PSG" />
**[[Bureau of Ships and Services/Legends|Bureau of Ships and Services]] was created,<ref name="EA" /> although alternative dates shortly after 18,000 BBY had been noted<ref name="PSG" />
*[[17,018 BBY]]<ref name="EGW" />
**The [[First Alsakan Conflict]] erupted with the Republic assault of [[Virujansi/Legends|Virujansi]]<ref name="EGW" />
**The end of the Great Manifest Period and the beginning of the [[Indecta Era]]<ref name="EA" /><ref name="NEC" />
**The writing system [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] began spreading throughout the galaxy<ref name="WW" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Great Manifest Period first appears in the [[2005]] publication ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.<ref name="NEC" /> It was given subsequent appearances in the sources ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> and ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''.<ref name="EA" /> Sources such as ''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]'',<ref name="CCW" /> ''[[Death in the Slave Pits of Lorrd]]'',<ref name="DSPL" /> and the ''Atlas'' provided background information regarding events within the Great Manifest Period, although only the latter mentions the era by name.<ref name="EA" /> The era of the Great Manifest Period is furthered in [[canon]] by ''[[Lords of the Expanse]]''<ref name="LotE" /> and ''[[Platt's Starport Guide]]'', both of which provide dates for events that fall within the period.<ref name="PSG" /><ref name="LotE" /> Lastly, the publication ''[[Challenge 66]]'', which is of ambiguous [[canon]]icity, includes events that take place within the early years of the Great Manifest Period.<ref name="C66-DF" /> In [[March]] [[2010]], the Great Manifest Period was given a mention in the [[in-universe]] article ''[[The Written Word]]'' by [[John Hazlett]], who used the in-universe persona of [[Doctor/Legends|Dr.]] [[Milanda Vorgan]].<ref name="WW" />

The end date of the Great Manifest Period was tied to the Alsakan Conflicts in ''The New Essential Chronology'' and ''The Essential Atlas'', which both stated that the historical period ended 17,000 BBY according to galactic historians.<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="EA" /> The publication of ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' in [[2012]] cast the starting date of the First Alsakan Crisis as 17,018 BBY. At the same time, however, ''Warfare'' does not mention such direct corrolation between the dates as the preceding publications.<ref name="EGW" /> Dates were drawn from combining the extant sources.

===Non-canon content===
About the time the Great Manifest Period began, a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] named [[Roni von Wasaki]] was born. He later became a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] who helped to maintain peace and stability in frontier sectors of the growing Republic. His strong influence caused many local [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]] to mark him with a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]]. While he fended off many [[Bounty hunter/Legends|who pursued him]], he was eventually captured by [[Leshy Drobo]] and [[XT-8]]. Wasaki was [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|frozen]] in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] and set aboard the [[Transport/Legends|transport]] ''[[Starkiller]]'' for travel. While being transported, however, the vessel's [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] failed. Wasaki remained trapped within the carbonite for 20,000 years, until the ''Starkiller'' was discovered.<ref name="C66-DF">{{ChallengeCite|66|Disturbance in the Force (article)}}</ref>
